svg.title: An AGV changes floors: what the pipeline does today
svg.desc: Animated, illustrative two-floor layout with one VRC. Step 0 shows the layout entries and the graph edges they create; step 1 the task planning (a plain TrayMove); step 2 SIPP driving AGV-1 across the VRC edge; steps 3 and 4 how the action graph collapses the ride and replaces it with VRC commands; step 5 the gaps.
svg.metadata: ["Layout. floors gives each floor a z; the two Lift nodes L3 (floor 0) and L13 (floor 1) share x and y; vrcs {id 1, root_node 3, nodes [3, 13]} makes them one VRC. Layout adds the 3-13 edge, PoseGraph files it under VRC_UP / VRC_DOWN by floor, and GarageGraph types it VRC_TRANSITION with length |3.2 - 0.0| = 3.2 m. The base state has the carriage at floor 1.", "Task planning. Moving T7 from P1 (floor 0) to P11 (floor 1) is an ordinary TrayMove carried by AGV-1, with its lift events. Stages 1-3 never look at floors or the carriage, and no VrcTransition event is created.", "Motion planning. SIPP drives AGV-1 P1 -> W2 -> L3 -> L13 -> W12 -> P11 and takes the VRC edge like any edge: 13.87 s of trapezoid travel over 3.2 m, no door time, no carriage. The plan does not know the carriage is on floor 1. The shaft rule keeps AGV-2 off L13 during the ride.", "Action graph, part 1. CollectAndCollapseTrajectoryMotions merges each run of floor-traversal motions into one motion (here a run of one): from the first source pose L3@90 to the next motion's source pose L13@90, with that next motion's action id. Each motion then becomes an AGV command.", "Action graph, part 2. InsertVrcActionsIntoDag simulates the carriage floor: it adds an approach VRC command to floor 0 before W2 -> L3, replaces the ride L3 -> L13 with a VRC move command to floor 1 (3 + 13.87 + 3 = 19.87 s each) and chains the VRC's users: approach, W2 -> L3, move, L13 -> W12.", "The gaps: the written VrcTransition planner is never called, SIPP's ride time is optimistic, the carriage is not an agent, a ride at the end of a trajectory is dropped, and task planning is not floor-aware."]
